index 151aeac3c..a45c45fbe 100644
--- a/src/type1/t1parse.c
+++ b/src/type1/t1parse.c
@@ -281,7 +281,7 @@
         if ( error )
           break;
 
-        if ( tag != 0x8002U || size > stream->size - stream->pos )
+        if ( tag != 0x8002U || size - 1 > stream->size - stream->pos )
           break;
 
         if ( FT_QREALLOC( priv_dict, priv_len, priv_len + size ) ||

coupling: The first edited commit introduces an in-memory fast path for PFB private-dictionary segments while retaining an explicit remaining-byte check, so that diff is safe by itself. The second edited commit changes only its centralized boundary expression; on the original tree, FT_STREAM_READ independently rejects an overlong segment, so that one-line diff is also safe by itself. During the actual maintenance sequence, the second commit centralizes validation and removes the first commit's local check, replacing it with size - 1 > remaining, which accepts a segment one byte longer than the stream contains. The unsafe direct copy is reached only when both edits are composed: the first commit supplies the unchecked memory-stream path and the second commit removes its guard while relaxing the replacement boundary. A correct repair must establish the shared invariant across both commits: the fast path and centralized check must use exactly the same stream-equivalent remaining-byte semantics. Adjusting one hunk without preserving that invariant can leave the other side unprotected.
